summary: Putin attends Olympics opening; "no limits" joint statement on international relations entering a new era issued.
First in-person meeting after the invasion of Ukraine; Putin publicly acknowledges Chinese "questions and concerns".
Xi state visit to Moscow; "new era" framing; joint statements on deepening partnership and on pre-2030 economic cooperation.
Xi cites "deepening trust"; Putin attends third Belt and Road Forum.
Putin's first trip of his new term; Joint Statement on Deepening the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership of Coordination for the New Era.
Xi state visit and guest of honour at the 9 May parade; joint statement on global strategic stability and joint declaration on upholding the authority of international law both signed 8 May.
Bilateral on the margins of the SCO summit.
Putin and Kim attend the Tiananmen military parade alongside Xi — first trilateral optics of this kind.
Lavrov visits Beijing; the two ministries sign the 2026 inter-MFA consultation plan. Agenda covered the US–Iran conflict, Asia-Pacific and Ukraine.

Putin's 25th visit to China; two joint statements — one on strengthening comprehensive strategic coordination and good-neighbourliness, one on advocating a multipolar world and a new type of international relations. Marks the 30th anniversary of the strategic partnership and the 25th of the Treaty of Good-Neighbourliness.
Regular FM meeting on the CFM margins; agenda included relations with the United States and the Ukraine crisis.
Bilateral on the margins of the Bishkek SCO summit; Xi says ties have grown "more solid"; Putin signals readiness to make the bilateral visa-free regime permanent.
Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang attends the Eastern Economic Forum and frames Northern Sea Route cooperation as raising both peoples' well-being.
